newsitem.title: UK: Kazminco to acquire precious/base licenses.
newsitem.headline: Kazminco to acquire precious/base licenses.

text.p: Kazakhstan Minerals Corp intends to become a major mining force in one of the world's least developed, mineral-rich regions, chairman Anthony Williams told the Global Emerging Markets '96 conference on Thursday.
"Being in Kazakhstan today is, we believe, comparable to investing in Peru or even Chile 10 short years ago," he said.
KazMinCo is set to acquire two exploration and development licences for territories in central Asian former Soviet republic by the end of the month.

The licences are for precious and base metals, covering an area of 27,000 square kilometres in the former Soviet republic, and provide for five years for exploration and 20 years for development on any discoveries.

KazMinCo, founded in 1993 with the aim to secure and develop mineral properties in Kazakhstan, has a market capitalisation of about $160 million and interests in nine joint ventures with Kazakh partners, Williams said.

"The macroeconomic outlook for some of these regions does not bear close examination but the advances in mineral expoloration and the sheer volume of territory being unlocked will inevitably lead to new discoveries," he added.

Williams said the company was to finish a pre-feasibility study of its Varvarinskoye gold deposit soon and aimed to start up a 120,000 ounce open pit operation next year. Initial open pit resources were indicated at one million ounces.

Drilling of its Samarskoye deposit indicated some 1.5 million tonnes of copper and over 2 million ounces of gold. The nearby Shokai deposit, a licence for which was acquired earlier this year, showed a similar structure.
"We believe we have identified a major new copper porphyry belt in Central Kazakstan," Williams said.
